newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: Satellite news most popular in Gulf - survey.
newsitem.headline: Satellite news most popular in Gulf - survey.

text.p: Gulf Arab students prefer foreign satellite television to local media for credible news, a survey in three countries published on Monday showed.
Questionnaires were sent to 500 students aged 14 to 22 in the three Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries of Kuwait, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates (UAE).

"In the three countries 75 percent of watchers of news prefer international networks, CNN and BBC. If incidents occur in the Gulf people tune in to the international channels," said Jamal al-Suwaidi, director of the Emirates Centre for Strategic Studies and Research.

"It appears that local news sources, including print and broadcast, are not really appreciated by the young of the GCC who instead prefer to watch CNN, NBC or listen to the BBC Arabic service -- about 75 percent of the students sampled said that foreign news services were more credible sources of information ...local sources of news are considered very poor," he said.
Results of the survey, published in UAE newspapers, were presented at the start on Sunday of a four-day conference on the impact of the information revolution on the Arab world.
The survey also found the average household in the three countries had three television sets and one video recorder.
Sport was the most popular television programme in Saudi Arabia, comedy in Kuwait and music in the UAE.
One UAE home had 868 telephone paging devices.
Use of the Internet was becoming widespread in Kuwait and the UAE but access was poor in Saudi Arabia, the survey added.
